Rows without `_src` are the 2026-06..08 harvest: fields learned from compiler output and validated by the round-trip census, not by per-field probes; their audit state is tracked in cubit's docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md (tools/audit_table.py, tools/audit_dynamic.py). `history` keeps the fix-wave notes that used to be loose `_meta.bugNNN` keys, verbatim; `errata` keeps the former top-level `_errata_*` notes (sm121a). `_meta.key_aliases` maps retired key names to the key that carries the rows today (cubit resolves them for text and lookups, never prints them).

qmma-sf-mxint8-silicon-2026-11-07.kind: undocumented form, measured on silicon; nvdisasm has no text for it
qmma-sf-mxint8-silicon-2026-11-07.silicon: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), test host GPU 0, 2026-11-07 09:50Z (session T-13): kernel needs44_types runs the five documented diagonal QMMA.SF.16832 type pairs and the 0x47e word on identical fragments (C = 0, scales 1.0). Byte-value sweeps of A (B = 0x0c / 0x40 / 0x38) and of B (A = the same): all 6 x 256 results of the 0x47e word equal 32 x (int8(v)/64) x (int8(w0)/64) exactly (0x7f -> 63.5 with B = 0x40, 0x80 -> -64.0, 0xff -> -0.5) — the OCP MXINT8 element map on both operands; the E4M3 / E5M2 / E3M2 / E2M3 / E2M1 / S8 / U8 maps do not fit. One-hot bytes light the 8 D elements of one row (A) / the 16 of one column (B) exactly as the E4M3.E4M3 row does (the m16n8k32 8-bit fragment layout); a byte is one element (0x04 -> 0.0625, 0x44 -> 1.0625). E8M0 scale sweep: D x 2^(s-127) for s = 0..254 (fp32 overflow to inf), NaN at 0xff. First measured 2026-11-06 (R): executes, fp32 output, scales honoured, arithmetic not E4M3 / E2M1 / integer. Replaces the 2026-03-26 hypothesis row IMMA.SF.16832.U8.U8_R_R_R_R_R_R_UR (no numerical oracle; operand model disagreed with the family). Harness: T/t13/needs44 (needs44_types.sass, needs44_run.py, out/needs44_results.json).
qmma-sf-mxint8-silicon-2026-11-07.note: Side result of the same run: the documented E2M1 type code computes exactly the E2M3 map on bits [5:0] of the 8-bit container for all 256 byte values (PTX places .e2m1 in bits [5:2] with zero padding — the silicon does not mask bits [1:0]); the E2M1 and E2M3 rows are therefore the same arithmetic on well-formed inputs.

nop.description: NOP — fully static, no write/wait mask allowed

s2r.description: System register read — hi[15:8] = SR code (opcode extension, not scheduling)

stg.description: Global memory store (descriptor form) — lower 32 all fixed, upper 32 has write/wait

sts.description: Shared memory store — hi[11:8]=0x8 is type discriminator

epoch_stg.comment: global store (write/wait in upper32 at non-standard offsets)

ldgsts_desc_forms_rebuild.alignment: 128-bit form requires 16B alignment of BOTH addresses (misalign = CUDA error 716)
ldgsts_desc_forms_rebuild.completion_semantics: completion is tracked per-instruction by the standard control-word write-barrier on the LDGSTS itself (consumer waits the slot; silicon-validated). The nvcc LDGDEPBAR/DEPBAR.LE group idiom does NOT function in bare cubins (DEPBAR.LE passes immediately; group counter inert - likely requires nvcc ELF/reservedSmem attributes) and is unnecessary. The 3x '@!PT LDS RZ,[RZ]' padding nvcc emits is not required for correctness (measured +1 cyc/iter). Descriptor out-of-bounds global reads land zeros (observed with gimm overflow)
ldgsts_desc_forms_rebuild.field_layout: lo32 = 0x0fae | guard<<12 | Rd(smem)<<16 | Ra(global,.64 pair)<<24; mid32 = gimm12(two's complement, +/-2KiB) | simm20<<12; hi32 = mod-consts | UR8 (descriptor)
ldgsts_desc_forms_rebuild.method: desc-form LDGSTS family rebuilt from an nvcc 13.0 sm_120 cp.async corpus (116 instructions, cuobjdump; asymmetric smem/global immediates discriminate every field) and validated by frozen-[CC] hardware probes on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (per-lane data round-trips for 4/8/16B forms, determinism x3, fresh process per variant)

shfl_regforms_pred_fix.note: dest-pred sits at bits[83:81] (PT=7); every harvested SHFL group had it baked into and_base as the AND across samples (usually 0 = P0), so assembling 'SHFL.UP PT, ...' silently encoded P0 and clobbered it at runtime. SHFL_P_R_R_R_II gained a DOWN group and its BFLY group was rebuilt from the reference encodings (the previous BFLY fields were a cross-contaminated harvest bucket shared with unrelated keys). Not touched: the remaining n=150 BFLY buckets (P_R_R_II_R, P_R_R_R_R) and the imm-b IDX keys (cross-contaminated harvests, no ground truth; they reject on the operand-completeness check instead of encoding garbage).
reference_encodings: SHFL.UP PT, R13, R0, R8, R9 = 0x04000008000d7389 (mode bit58)

stallfix.comment: SM120 v3 rules, measured 2026-11-03 on 4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition (cubit session T, harness stallfloor_gen.py v2: one cubit-assembled kernel per (path, distance d, producer stall S), producer and consumer d one-cycle fillers apart, every other edge at S15 or behind a scoreboard, 256 pairs per thread, 32 CTAs x 1 024 threads x 20 repetitions; a reference kernel per path with the tested edge behind scoreboard 0 proves the CPU model before a floor is read; floor = smallest S with 0 mismatching threads such that every larger S is clean). Floors (path d0/d1/d2): rpath 4/0/0, xchain 4/0/0, urpath 4/3/0 -> floor_global 4 (R1/R7) + floor_urpath_d1 3; pcarry (ISETP -> SEL reading the predicate) 5/4/0 -> floor_pcarry_d0/d1 (R11, a predicate read as data); dmix (IMAD.WIDE.U32 cout -> IADD3.X cin) 5/0/0; guard (ISETP -> @P0 IADD3) d0: 13 (v4, 2026-11-05: the v3 sweep ended at S11 where 641 888 / 655 360 threads were still wrong; harness v4 swept S12..S15: S12 618 880 wrong, S13/S14/S15 clean) -> floor_guard_d0 13, guard_d0_forbid false; the new guardbra path (ISETP -> @P0 BRA over the effect instruction) measured the same law 13 / 11 / 9; d1 = 11 (the single clean value measured, S10 = 643 744 wrong) -> floor_guard_d1 11 for every consumer class (guard_d1_forbid false; the sm_103a class split was not measured here); d2 = 9; xread (UIADD3 UR -> vector IADD3) 6/4/2; uguard (UISETP -> @UP0 UIADD3) 10/8/6; mufu (MUFU.RCP -> FFMA): no stall 1..11 closes it at any distance (variable latency: the scoreboard is the only legal schedule, as on sm_103a; the pass never touches barriers); r2ur: NOT measured - the harness's CPU model disagreed with the scoreboarded reference (24 576 of 32 768 threads: R2UR takes one lane's value, the model summed per-thread values), the corrected kernel is queued; until it runs floor_r2ur_d0 = cap (raise-only to the maximum legal stall, never a smaller guess). S00 was clean on every path at every distance including MUFU: on sm_120 a stall count of 0 behaves as a hardware interlock, not as 'no stall'; it is not used as a floor (the pass never writes S00). cap_stall 15 (v4): S12..S15 without yield execute and were measured as floors on both SKUs; S12-15 with yield are decoder-reserved on SM120 (docs/SM120_CONTROL_OPEX.md), without yield unmeasured. | 2026-11-04 (4x RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition, harness v3 r2ur kernels with warp-uniform inputs, model_r2ur PASS, 26 floors PASS on every path): r2ur measured 4/0/0 -> floor_r2ur_d0 4 (== floor_global; R2UR broadcasts one lane, the v2 model that summed per-thread values was wrong, now corrected). KNOWN_ISSUES A3 closed in full.
